arxiv-2212-06430.title: Can recurrent neural networks learn process model structure?
arxiv-2212-06430.creator: Jari Peeperkorn, Seppe vanden Broucke, Jochen De Weerdt
arxiv-2212-06430.description: Abstract Various methods using machine and deep learning have been proposed to tackle different tasks in predictive process monitoring, forecasting for an ongoing case e.g. the most likely next event or suffix, its remaining time, or an outcome-related variable. Recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and more specifically long short-term memory nets (LSTMs), stand out in terms of popularity.

arxiv-2312-04749.creator: Simon Luo, Adrian Herrera, Paul Quirk, Michael Chase, Damith C. Ranasinghe, Salil S. Kanhere
arxiv-2312-04749.description: Abstract . Fuzzing is an industry-standard software testing technique that uncovers bugs in a target program by executing it with mutated inputs. Over the lifecycle of a fuzzing campaign, the fuzzer accumulates inputs inducing new and interesting target behaviors, drawing from these inputs for further mutation and generation of new inputs.

arxiv-2403-06621.description: Abstract Humans use UAVs to monitor changes in forest environments since they are lightweight and provide a large variety of surveillance data. pmc-11624395.title: Commercial perspectives: Genome editing as a breeding tool for health and well-being in dairy cattle*
pmc-11624395.creator: Tad S Sonstegard, Julio M Flórez, José Fernando Garcia
pmc-11624395.description: Graphical AbstractSummary: Conventional breeding methods have driven genetic progress in cattle. Genome editing, a novel breeding technique, can expedite the introduction of desirable traits into elite genetics in a single generation. Gene editing-mediated introgression of alleles has commonly been done with single-cell embryos, albeit often accompanied by the occurrence of mosaicism.

pmc-11690477.title: A STORM IS COMING: A CLIMATE RESILIENCE FRAMEWORK FOR SENIOR HOUSING
pmc-11690477.creator: Taylor Patskanick, Grace Turner, Joseph Coughlin
pmc-11690477.description: Older adults’ vulnerability to extreme weather events may vary especially based on geographic location and housing or residential situation. Emergency preparedness is a potentially modifiable protective factor influencing this vulnerability. Emergency preparedness, however, looks different for older adults living in senior housing communities compared to community-dwelling older adults.

pmc-12466666.title: Long-Term Exercise Interventions for Reducing Drug Craving in People with Drug Use Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-12466666.creator: Xiang Chen, Yuanyuan Jia, Ping Hong, Tingting Sun, Xiaosheng Dong, Jinghua Qian, Junwei Qian, Xiao Hou, Chella Kamarajan, Yingzhi Lu
pmc-12466666.description: Exercise is a promising intervention for reducing drug craving, but recent studies have shown inconsistent effects. This meta-analysis aims to evaluate the effect of exercise interventions on drug craving and identify the key exercise factors that affect its effectiveness. The literature was searched in four English databases. Two authors independently performed literature screening, data extraction, and quality assessment.

pmc-13314155.title: Comparative analysis of delayed ovulation and associated ovarian patterns in the Ongole crossbred cattle
pmc-13314155.creator: Herdis Herdis, Langgeng Priyanto, Santoso Santoso, Fitra Aji Pamungkas, Rahma Isartina Anwar, Desiana Ade Mahari, Florentina Bety Indah Lupitasari, Nurul Azizah, Anita Hafid, Reski Amalia, Ligaya Ita Tumbelaka, Amrozi Amrozi, Pradita Iustitia Sitaresmi
pmc-13314155.description: Background:Delayed ovulation can have harmful effects on cattle reproduction, especially in countries that rely on artificial insemination, resulting in significant economic losses, as evidenced by Indonesia.Aim:This study provides novel insights into hormone dynamics and ovarian environment comparisons in delayed ovulation (DO) and Normal cows (NO) cows.Methods:Eight Ongole-crossbred cows with DO or NO over four estrous cycles were observed.
